passage:
Sunday
Two offers, and I've gone round in circles for three days. Tonight I did what Minakshi suggested: a proper table.
Five things: learning, pay, commute, team, stability. First I gave each a weight out of 5 based on what I actually care about now, not what sounds impressive. Learning 5. Team 4. Commute 3. Pay 3. Stability 2, because I live with my parents and can take some risk.
Then I scored both offers out of 10.
Big firm: learning 6, team 6, commute 5, pay 8, stability 9.
Small product company: learning 8, team 7, commute 6, pay 6, stability 5.
Multiplied and added. Big firm: 111. Small company: 114.
So the small company edges ahead. Only just. But what surprised me was the feeling when I saw it: relief. I think I wanted it to win all along.
Indu

Monday. Pranav had two offers, one from a consulting firm in Gurugram and one from a mid-sized software company in his home city, Lucknow. He wrote a pros-and-cons list in his notebook. Gurugram: bigger name, faster growth, "my kind of people". Lucknow: home food, slower pace. He read it back and shrugged. It said what he already felt: Gurugram.
Wednesday. His friend Disha, who had moved to Gurugram last year, read the list on a video call. "Where's rent? The deposit? The broker's fee? Your metro card?" Pranav hadn't written a single cost. They added them up together. It came to almost two months of his first salary, before he'd even started.
Saturday. Pranav rewrote the list with a new heading, "Moving costs", and called both HR teams to ask about joining support. The Gurugram firm offered a small relocation amount. He still leaned toward Gurugram, but now with open eyes.

Did the thing I was scared of: messaged strangers.
Found two people on the professional networking site: Zeenat, a junior analyst at the insurance company for a year, and Rohit, at the fintech start-up for eight months. Short messages: who I am, which offer, could I ask three questions in 15 minutes?
Both said yes!
Same three questions to each: What's a normal week's workload? What have you learned in your first year? How do appraisals really work?
Zeenat: 9 to 6, rarely later; formal training for three months; appraisal once a year, clear ratings.
Rohit: honest guy. Said 50-hour weeks are normal, learning is huge but self-taught, and appraisals "happen when the founder remembers."
None of this was in either offer letter.
I don't know yet which I'll pick. But now I'm choosing between two real jobs, not two PDFs.
Bhavna

qa.q: What else could Payal do if HR had confirmed Noida?
qa.a: Payal could then reconsider calmly, weighing the new location against the offer, and ask HR about options before deciding.

qa.q: How does Aparna help?
qa.a: Aparna stays calm and asks where the message came from, which stops Payal reacting to a rumour.

grounding: Shows a candidate who hears after accepting that the joining location may change asking HR to confirm in writing and planning to reconsider only if it differs.

subtype: Approach: revising after new information [Revision]
passage: Mehak was standing at the Dadar bus stop when the HR executive called. "Just letting you know, your joining location will be Chennai, not Mumbai." It was said so casually that Mehak almost said okay. Instead she asked, "Could you please send that to me in writing, with the reason and whether it's permanent?" That evening, over pav bhaji with her friend Ira, she opened the email. It confirmed Chennai, for at least the whole first year. "So?" Ira asked. Mehak took out her notebook. She had chosen this company over another Mumbai offer partly because of home: no rent, Aai's cooking, her little brother's exams. With Chennai, that part had changed. "I'm not going to ignore it," she said. "I'm not going to panic either. I'll compare again, honestly, with the new facts." She drew two columns and started.

qa.q: Where was Mehak when HR called?
qa.a: At the Dadar bus stop.

qa.q: How did Mehak feel on reading the written confirmation?
qa.a: Mehak was unsettled but calm, determined neither to ignore it nor to panic.

qa.q: What else could Mehak do while comparing again?
qa.a: Mehak could ask HR whether a move back to Mumbai is possible later, and check whether the other Mumbai offer is still open, before deciding.

qa.q: How might Ira see Mehak's reaction?
qa.a: Ira sees Mehak handle surprising news steadily, getting it in writing and planning to decide with the new facts.

grounding: Illustrates a candidate who, told after accepting that the joining location has moved, asks HR to confirm in writing and reconsiders because the answer differs.
